title: Groupoïdes de Teichmüller et les S0 Tg,!ν, S0 TG : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: Grothendieck is building a combinatorial calculus of 'MD-graphs' (modular dual graphs). These are what are now called stable graphs, i.e. dual graphs of stable pointed curves. Each one has a vertex set S, a set of oriented edges A⃗ with a fixed-point-free involution (written α ↦ -α), an origin map σ: A⃗ → S, a set of free half-edges or legs I, and genus weights g: S → ℕ. Together A^ = I ⊔ A⃗. The graph indexes boundary strata M_G of the compactified moduli stack M̄_{g,ν}.

On the previous page he defined a 'homomorphism of generalization' u: G → G'. It consists of maps u_s: S → S' and u_a: A⃗ → A^' ⊔ S'. The edges C⃗ sent to vertices are contracted, and the other edges B⃗ are mapped bijectively. The genus condition is g_{s'} = Σ_{s ∈ u^{-1}(s')} g_s + h^1(G_0(s')).

This page makes the observation that such a G' is determined, up to unique isomorphism, by G together with the set C ⊂ A(G) of 'bound' (contracted) edges. The explicit construction is:
- G_{0C} is the subgraph with all vertices S and oriented edges C⃗, the preimage of C, keeping the weights g.
- S' = π_0(G_{0C}).
- A^' = A^ \ C⃗.
- The origin map σ' is the composite A^' ↪ A^ → S → π_0(G_{0C}); the involution is induced.
- g_{s'} is the virtual genus of the component G_{0C,s'}, namely Σ g_s + h^1.

In modern terms, G' = G/C is the edge contraction of a stable graph along a set of edges. Geometrically it is the specialization relation between boundary strata: the stratum of G lies in the closure of the stratum of G/C, since smoothing the nodes in C 'generalizes' the curve.

A second NB records the invariants that are preserved:
- the legs, I ≅ I';
- the connected components, π_0(G) ≅ π_0(G');
- the virtual genus of each connected component, γ = γ'.
These are the facts that contraction preserves the type (g, ν) of each connected component.

The next page goes on to the dual operation of 'découpage' (cutting edges into pairs of legs, i.e. partial normalization) and to ordinary and induction homomorphisms.
errors: No mathematical error. Small notational points: the origin map is called σ here (and 'σ' induced by σ' twice is redundant). G' is defined only up to unique isomorphism, as stated. The stability of G' is not checked explicitly, but it follows: the valence of a contracted vertex plus 2·(virtual genus) only grows, so the stability inequality is preserved.

ideas.what: Contraction of a weighted stable graph along a set C of edges. New vertices are π_0 of the subgraph spanned by C; new genus is the virtual genus Σg_s + h^1 of each component; the remaining half-edges are kept.
ideas.modern_name: edge contraction G → G/C of stable graphs (morphisms in the category of stable graphs; specialization of boundary strata of M̄_{g,n})
ideas.usually_credited_to: Implicit in Deligne–Mumford/Knudsen dual graphs. Formalized as morphisms of stable graphs by Kontsevich–Manin (1994), Behrend–Manin (1996) and Getzler–Kapranov (modular operads, 1998); used systematically by Arbarello–Cornalba.
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses the stratification of M̄_{g,ν} and the Teichmüller tower informally, without this formalism.

ideas.what: Invariance under contraction of the legs, the connected components and the genus of each component.
ideas.modern_name: contraction preserves the type (g, n) of a stable graph
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore / the same sources as above

missed.claim: A precursor of the category of stable graphs with contraction morphisms (the 'generalization homomorphisms'), together with a separate notion of 'découpage' (cutting) and induction morphisms on the next page. It is written down by Grothendieck (dated from 1978 on) about 15 years before Kontsevich–Manin and Getzler–Kapranov formalized it. The content itself is standard today.
missed.quote: Le MD-graphe G' se déduit, à isom. unique près, de G et de C (⊂ A = A(G))
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical priority only: it documents that Grothendieck had a combinatorial graph-category formalism for the strata of M̄_{g,ν} as part of the Teichmüller groupoid project. No new mathematics for specialists.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful, correct, but routine definition of edge contraction for stable graphs. It is mainly of historical interest as an early, unpublished formalization of the stable-graph category.
